t: Born in a log cabin in Kentucky and largely self-educated, Lincoln became a lawyer and Illinois legislator and returned to politics in 1854 to oppose the spread of slavery into the territories.

Elected in 1860 as the first Republican president, he took executive control of the Union's war against the seceded Confederate states, and on January 1, 1863, declared the slaves in the states in rebellion to be free.
He was shot five days after the Confederate surrender at Appomattox; later ages have honoured him as a martyr and the Great Emancipator, and some have disputed that title.
dyk: In 1849 Lincoln received a patent for a flotation device for moving riverboats in shallow water. It was never commercialized, but it made him the only president to hold a patent.
ev: Lincoln is born in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky
In his second campaign he wins a seat in the Illinois House of Representatives, where he serves four terms
He is elected to the U.S. House of Representatives as the only Whig in the Illinois delegation
He holds seven debates with Stephen A. Douglas in the Illinois Senate campaign; the legislature re-elects Douglas
He is elected the first Republican president with 39.8 percent of the vote in a four-way race, and South Carolina adopts an ordinance of secession
He issues the final Emancipation Proclamation on January 1 and delivers the Gettysburg Address on November 19
He is re-elected with 55.1 percent of the popular vote and 212 electoral votes to George B. McClellan's 21
John Wilkes Booth shoots him at Ford's Theatre on April 14, and he dies the next morning

f.born: February 12, 1809, in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky, near Hodgenville; second child of Thomas Lincoln and Nancy Hanks Lincoln, a frontier farming family
f.died: April 15, 1865, at Petersen House in Washington, D.C., nine hours after being shot in the head by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre
f.role: Member of the Illinois House of Representatives (four terms from 1834); U.S. representative from Illinois (1847–1849); lawyer; 16th president of the United States (1861–1865)
f.known: leading the Union in the American Civil War; the Emancipation Proclamation of 1863; the Gettysburg Address; promoting the Thirteenth Amendment abolishing slavery; the debates with Stephen A. Douglas in 1858; being the first U.S. president to be assassinated
